value.rationale: The six-cell grid is the first three-repeat alternation after the degenerate two-repeat four-cell case; a sharp, arbitrary-contrast boundary proves necessity of a classical sufficient mesh restriction where it is not guaranteed generally. Two structural negative off-diagonal witnesses furnish a complete finite-model classification relevant to graded periodic finite-element testing. It is not a generic determinant exercise with arbitrary parameters; its parameters are physical element lengths and timestep.
